claims.text: Spin-polarized DFT+U can reliably predict the emergence of ferromagnetic ground states in materials with strongly correlated d or f electrons.
Appropriate Hubbard U values for transition-metal systems are typically between 3 and 6 eV.
Standard DFT may fail to indicate robust magnetic ordering in transition-metal oxides because it underestimates electron-correlation effects.
A Hubbard U correction can be introduced into spin-polarized DFT to investigate magnetic ground states at 0 K.
The proposed method applies to materials with localized d or f electrons and significant electron correlations.
Localized d or f electronic states promote exchange interactions through enhanced electron-correlation effects.
The on-site Coulomb interaction represented by U increases the exchange splitting of localized electronic states.
Increased exchange splitting stabilizes a ferromagnetic arrangement relative to nonmagnetic or antiferromagnetic arrangements.
For a ferromagnetic ground state, DFT+U calculations will yield a lower total energy for the ferromagnetic configuration than for competing magnetic configurations.
The predicted ferromagnetic configuration will have a significant magnetic moment.
Standard spin-polarized DFT without a Hubbard U correction can fail to capture the correct magnetic ordering because it treats local electron-electron interactions insufficiently.
DFT+U is expected to be effective when electronic states are strongly localized.
The method may be limited when electron correlations are weak.
The method may be limited when the appropriate U value is ambiguous.
Predicted magnetic ordering can be sensitive to the selected U parameter.
Experimental validation is required to confirm the predictive capability of DFT+U for ferromagnetic ordering.
